name: Lightning Caller

gist.Sol Rym, the Thunder Djinn: Casts Chain Lightning regardless of its level, from the first turn. Can only ever take one action per turn and has very little health.
gist.Chain Lightning: You must choose three of your own targets, heroes first: a heavy hit, a medium one, a lighter one. With three heroes and no creatures, every cast lands on all of them.
gist.Butterfly Cloud: Light damage to your whole side, and its caster cannot be chosen by you until his next turn.
gist.Fiona, the Princess of Blackport: Gains a pile of gold whenever she is afflicted by a status effect, including the ones he moves onto her himself.
gist.Nicolas, the Hidden Alchemist: Potion draws; potions in the main deck.
gist.Snow Cannon: Freezes one of your targets for a turn; four copies.
gist.Renewable Energy: Shuffles three spent cards (the Chain Lightnings) back into his deck.
gist.Tea: Moves status effects from one of his targets to another, usually onto Fiona for gold.
gist.Tool Freezer: Reaction: cancels an artifact you play.
gist.Smug Coin: Equipment: once per game its hero survives a lethal hit on a sliver.
gist.Divine Gift of Rain: Once per game: cancels a card or effect that would affect his side.
gist.MOE Bomb: Destroys every creature on the board.
gist.Punch in the Box: Reaction potion: half of a hit on his side is thrown back.
gist.Golden Ankh: Revives a hero for a turn: one more Chain Lightning from Sol Rym. Four copies.

plan: North Crown's ace does one thing from the first turn: Sol Rym casts Chain Lightning. The spell makes you choose three of your own targets, heroes first, and a deck with three heroes and no creatures takes all three hits every time. Leadership, Magnetic Glove and Wheels find the next copy, Renewable Energy shuffles them back, four Snow Cannons keep your caster frozen, and four Golden Ankhs bring Sol Rym back for one more cast each. Everything rests on one very fragile hero who can take a single action per turn; the other two do not attack at all.

looks.early: Sol Rym casting on turn one; all three of your heroes already hurt.
looks.mid: A Chain Lightning every turn, your caster frozen, a Smug Coin on Sol Rym.
looks.late: Sol Rym revived for the third time, your heroes on their last legs, his deck reshuffled with the same four spells.

opening.tell: Sol Rym has cast Chain Lightning on the first turn and has barely any health.
opening.why: He is the only hero who can cast it and the smallest on the table: every point of damage goes at him now; a slow setup means taking three hits a turn while you build.

midgame.tell: Each Chain Lightning hits all three of your heroes, the first one hardest; he controls no creatures.
midgame.why: You choose the order: put the heavy hit on the hero with Cloud in a Bottle or Firewall (which burns Sol Rym back) and keep finishing him; there is nothing to sweep.

crisis.tell: Sol Rym wears a Smug Coin and Rex holds Golden Ankhs; each revival is one more cast.
crisis.why: Stop the casts rather than the caster: The White Eye discards the Chain Lightning from his hand, and a frozen Sol Rym loses his single action; building further is pointless under this clock.

endgame.tell: His Golden Ankhs are spent and the other two heroes have never attacked.
endgame.why: Without Sol Rym the deck has almost no damage; Fiona and Nicolas simply need to be finished.
